youtube.summary: Simon O’Connor speaks with National MP Melissa Lee about the importance of every vote, following her extraordinary 18-vote loss in the 2023 election. She discusses the need for better voter education, particularly among ethnic communities, her work representing New Zealand’s diverse communities, and the changing political landscape in Mount Albert ahead of the next election. youtube.title: PROF GRANT SCHOFIELD
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan talks with public health expert Grant Schofield about New Zealand's deepening healthcare crisis, from GP shortages and ambulance delays to the election parties' health policies. Using Henry Ford's “faster horses” analogy, Schofield argues most parties are simply expanding an overwhelmed system rather than tackling preventable chronic disease, and calls for billions redirected into genuine prevention and flipped financial incentives in primary care. Discover more on the Make New Zealand Healthy website Or find them on Facebook , X and Telegram For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday.

youtube.title: SONIA ELIJAH
youtube.summary: British investigative journalist Sonia Elijah examines what Anthony Fauci, Pfizer and regulators knew about potential pregnancy risks from the Covid mRNA shots. She discusses Fauci’s January 2021 texts and diary entries, Pfizer’s pregnancy and lactation safety documents, reports of miscarriage and other adverse pregnancy outcomes, and a study of more than 220,000 pregnancies in Israel. For more information: Sonia's substack | Sonia Elijah Investigates Sonia's interview on RCR in May 2023 | Sonia Elijah on the Pfizer Safety Report for Pregnancy & Lactation Jeffrey Tucker of the Brownstone Institute recently on RCR | What Fauci’s Diaries Reveal Stories you won’t see on the 6pm news — RCR Bites, delivered FREE every weekday.

youtube.title: IRENA ZAGLADOV
youtube.summary: Michael Arbon talks with South Australian local councillor and Liberal Women's Council president Irena Zagladov about the failed Childhood Gender Dysphoria Amendment Bill, arguing puberty blockers for minors lack evidence and that parents, not the state, should hold primary decision-making power. Drawing on her upbringing in Soviet Ukraine, she links growing state involvement in children's care to Marxist ideology and discusses the recently recommitted Parental Primacy Bill and the Senate's rejection of a motion affirming parental authority over social media bans. Discover more from Irena Zagladov on Facebook and Instagram , and the Liberal Women's Council The stories you won’t find on the 6pm news — RCR Bites , FREE every weekday
